records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם לֶךְ־לְךָ֛ מֵאַרְצְךָ֥ וּמִמּֽוֹלַדְתְּךָ֖ וּמִבֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַרְאֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: And said YHWH to Abram, go, for yourself, from your land and from your kindred and from the house of your father, to the land that I will show you.
pieces: Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives and your father's household, and go to the land I will show you.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Go out from your land and from your kindred and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.

R.1: One day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives and your father's family. Go to the land that I will show you.

decisions.choice: go out (lekh lekha): go, for your own sake
decisions.reason: The command is "go" with "for yourself" added, which strengthens it: set out, leave. The same words begin the test of 22:2 ("go to the land of Moriah"), framing Abraham's story.

decisions.choice: your land, your kindred, your father's house: leaving everything that gave security
decisions.reason: The list narrows from country to clan to family. In that world a person's land and family were his protection and identity. Abram is to leave them for a land he has not seen, trusting God's word (Hebrews 11:8).

decisions.choice: the land that I will show you: not yet named
decisions.reason: God does not name the land; Abram is to go and be shown. The narrator has already told the reader it is Canaan (11:31).

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} calls Abram

records.source: וְאֶֽעֶשְׂךָ֙ לְג֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל וַאֲבָ֣רֶכְךָ֔ וַאֲגַדְּלָ֖ה שְׁמֶ֑ךָ וֶהְיֵ֖ה בְּרָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will make you into a nation great, and I will bless you and make great your name, and be a blessing.
pieces: I will make a great nation of you. I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.

L.2: And I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be a blessing.

R.2: I will make your family into a great nation. I will bless you and make you famous, and you will be a blessing to others.

decisions.choice: a great nation: from a childless man
decisions.reason: God promises a great nation to a man whose wife is barren (11:30). The promise of descendants runs through the whole of Abraham's story.

decisions.choice: I will make your name great: God gives what Babel tried to seize
decisions.reason: The builders of Babel said, "let us make a name for ourselves" (11:4). Here God promises Abram a great name as a gift.

decisions.choice: and be a blessing: so that you will be a blessing
decisions.reason: The verb is a command in form, but after the promises it expresses their purpose and result: Abram will be a blessing to others. The word "bless" comes five times in verses 2-3, answering the five curses of chapters 3-11.

records.source: וַאֲבָֽרֲכָה֙ מְבָ֣רְכֶ֔יךָ וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ֖ אָאֹ֑ר וְנִבְרְכ֣וּ בְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I will bless [those] blessing you, and [the one] treating you lightly I will curse; and will be blessed in you all [the] clans of the ground.
pieces: I will bless those who bless you, and whoever treats you with contempt I will curse; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you."

L.3: And I will bless those who bless you, and the one who treats you with contempt I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth will be blessed."

R.3: I will bless people who are kind to you. Anyone who treats you badly, I will curse. And through you, all the families on earth will be blessed."

decisions.choice: treats you with contempt ... I will curse: two different words
decisions.reason: The first verb (qalal) means to treat lightly, to belittle; the second (arar) is the word for a solemn curse. Those who blessed are plural, the one who belittles is singular: blessing is to be the rule, and cursing the exception.

decisions.choice: in you all the families of the earth will be blessed
alternatives: by you all the families of the earth will bless themselves (use your name in blessing)
decisions.reason: The verb form can be passive ("will be blessed") or reflexive ("will bless themselves", that is, will say "may God bless us as he blessed Abram"). The Septuagint and the New Testament read it as passive: God's blessing will reach all peoples through Abram (Acts 3:25; Galatians 3:8). The promise answers the scattering of the nations in chapters 10-11.

decisions.choice: families of the earth: the clans of all humankind
decisions.reason: The word for families is the one used for the clans of the nations in chapter 10 (10:5, 32).

records.source: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אַבְרָ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ ל֑וֹט וְאַבְרָ֗ם בֶּן־חָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּצֵאת֖וֹ מֵחָרָֽן׃
records.gloss: And went Abram as had spoken to him YHWH, and went with him Lot; and Abram [was] a son of five and seventy year[s] when he went out from Haran.
pieces: Abram set out as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran.

L.4: So Abram went, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram [was] seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

R.4: So Abram left, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

decisions.choice: Abram went, as the LORD had told him: obedience without question
decisions.reason: Abram's response is told in a few words: he goes. No reply is recorded, only obedience, as with Noah (6:22). Hebrews 11:8 calls it faith: "he went out, not knowing where he was going".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אַבְרָם֩ אֶת־שָׂרַ֨י אִשְׁתּ֜וֹ וְאֶת־ל֣וֹט בֶּן־אָחִ֗יו וְאֶת־כָּל־רְכוּשָׁם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָכָ֔שׁוּ וְאֶת־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־עָשׂ֣וּ בְחָרָ֑ן וַיֵּצְא֗וּ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And took Abram Sarai his wife and Lot, [the] son of his brother, and all their possessions which they had gathered, and the persons whom they had acquired in Haran, and they went out to go to [the] land of Canaan; and they came to [the] land of Canaan.
pieces: Abram took with him his wife Sarai, his brother's son Lot, everything they owned and the people who had become part of their household in Haran. They set out for Canaan and reached it.

L.5: And Abram took Sarai his wife and Lot his brother's son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people that they had acquired in Haran, and they set out to go to the land of Canaan; and they came to the land of Canaan.

R.5: Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, everything they owned and all the servants they had gained in Haran. They set out for the land of Canaan, and they arrived there.

decisions.choice: the people they had acquired: servants and slaves
decisions.reason: "Persons" (nefesh) here means people who belonged to the household, such as servants and slaves; "acquired" is literally "made", used of gaining wealth (31:1). An old Jewish reading took it to mean people Abram and Sarai had won to faith in God, but the context is the household's possessions.

decisions.choice: they came to the land of Canaan: Terah's journey completed
decisions.reason: Terah set out for Canaan but stopped at Haran (11:31). Abram completes the journey.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Readable says "servants" for the members of the household (m1). Since the text does not say whether they were hired servants or slaves, the general word is used.

records.source: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אַבְרָם֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ עַ֚ד מְק֣וֹם שְׁכֶ֔ם עַ֖ד אֵל֣וֹן מוֹרֶ֑ה וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י אָ֥ז בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And passed through Abram in the land as far as [the] place of Shechem, as far as [the] great tree of Moreh; and the Canaanite[s] then [were] in the land.
pieces: Abram passed through the country as far as Shechem and the great tree of Moreh. In those days the Canaanites lived in the land.

L.6: And Abram passed through the land as far as the place of Shechem, as far as the great tree of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites [were] in the land.

R.6: Abram traveled through the land until he came to a place called Shechem, to the big tree of Moreh. The Canaanites were living in the land at that time.

decisions.choice: the place of Shechem: a holy site in the hill country
decisions.reason: Shechem, in the center of the land between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, later became an important city and a place of covenant (Joshua 24:1, 25). "The place" may mean a holy place.

decisions.choice: the great tree of Moreh: a large tree, perhaps an oak or terebinth
decisions.reason: The word means a large, sacred-looking tree, an oak or terebinth. Moreh may mean "teacher" or "oracle-giver": perhaps a tree where people sought guidance.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites were then in the land: the promised land was already occupied
decisions.reason: The note explains that the land God is about to promise to Abram's descendants (verse 7) was already the home of others; the promise will be fulfilled only much later (15:13-16).

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְזַ֨רְעֲךָ֔ אֶתֵּ֖ן אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וַיִּ֤בֶן שָׁם֙ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ לַיהוָ֖ה הַנִּרְאֶ֥ה אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And appeared YHWH to Abram and said, to your offspring I will give this land. And he built there an altar to YHWH, who had appeared to him.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your descendants." So Abram built an altar there to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who had appeared to him.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." And he built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who had appeared to him.

R.7: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your children and their children." So Abram built an altar there to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who had appeared to him.

decisions.choice: the LORD appeared: the first time God is said to appear to someone
decisions.reason: The verb means "let himself be seen". The text does not describe how God appeared; the point is that God came to Abram and spoke in the land itself.

decisions.choice: to your offspring I will give this land: the promise of the land
decisions.reason: "Offspring" is the word "seed", the word of 3:15. The land is promised to Abram's descendants, not to Abram himself, and he has no child yet. The promise is repeated and widened in 13:14-17 and 15:18.

decisions.choice: he built an altar: claiming the land for the LORD
decisions.reason: Abram builds altars at the places God leads him (verse 8; 13:18), worshiping the LORD in a land of Canaanite shrines.

records.source: וַיַּעְתֵּ֨ק מִשָּׁ֜ם הָהָ֗רָה מִקֶּ֛דֶם לְבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וַיֵּ֣ט אָהֳלֹ֑הבֵּֽית־אֵ֤ל מִיָּם֙ וְהָעַ֣י מִקֶּ֔דֶם וַיִּֽבֶן־שָׁ֤ם מִזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֖א בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he moved from there to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, Bethel from [the] west and Ai from [the] east; and he built there an altar to YHWH and called on [the] name of YHWH.
pieces: From there he moved on into the hills east of Bethel and set up his tent between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. He built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} there and called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.8: And he moved on from there to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and he built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.8: From there Abram moved to the hills east of the town of Bethel. He set up his tent between Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built another altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Bethel and Ai: towns in the central hill country
decisions.reason: Bethel ("house of God") is named by the name it had later; Jacob gives it this name in 28:19. Ai ("the ruin") lies to its east (Joshua 7-8).

decisions.choice: called on the name of the LORD: worship, as in 4:26
decisions.reason: Abram worships the LORD by name, as the line of Seth did (4:26).

records.source: וַיִּסַּ֣ע אַבְרָ֔ם הָל֥וֹךְ וְנָס֖וֹעַ הַנֶּֽגְבָּה׃פ
records.gloss: And journeyed Abram, going and journeying, toward the Negev.
pieces: Then Abram set out and kept moving on toward the Negev.

L.9: And Abram journeyed on, going on and on toward the Negev.

R.9: Then Abram kept moving south toward the desert of the Negev.

decisions.choice: the Negev: the dry land in the south
decisions.reason: The word means "the dry" or "the south": the dry region in the south of the land, between the hill country and the Sinai desert.

decisions.choice: going and journeying: moving on in stages
decisions.reason: Two verbs together describe travel by stages, moving camp from place to place.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י רָעָ֖ב בָּאָ֑רֶץ וַיֵּ֨רֶד אַבְרָ֤ם מִצְרַ֨יְמָה֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם כִּֽי־כָבֵ֥ד הָרָעָ֖ב בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And was a famine in the land, and went down Abram to Egypt to sojourn there, for heavy [was] the famine in the land.
pieces: But famine struck the land, so severe that Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a time.

L.10: And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to live there as a foreigner, for the famine [was] severe in the land.

R.10: But there was no food in the land of Canaan. The famine was so bad that Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while.

decisions.choice: to sojourn: to live as a foreigner for a time
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live in a land as a resident foreigner, without the rights of a citizen. Israel later describes its fathers in this way (Deuteronomy 26:5).

decisions.choice: famine, a descent to Egypt: a pattern repeated in Jacob's day
decisions.reason: Egypt, watered by the Nile, often had food when Canaan did not. The story foreshadows the later descent of Jacob's family to Egypt in famine (chapters 42-46) and the exodus.

records.heading: Abram and Sarai in Egypt

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִקְרִ֖יב לָב֣וֹא מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־שָׂרַ֣י אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִשָּׁ֥ה יְפַת־מַרְאֶ֖ה אָֽתְּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, when he drew near to enter Egypt, and he said to Sarai his wife, behold, please, I know that a woman beautiful of appearance [are] you.
pieces: Just before they reached Egypt, Abram said to his wife Sarai, "Listen. I know you are a beautiful woman.

L.11: And it happened, as he drew near to enter Egypt, that he said to Sarai his wife, "Look, I know that you [are] a beautiful woman.

R.11: As they came near to Egypt, Abram said to his wife Sarai, "You are a very beautiful woman.

decisions.choice: look, please: a polite appeal
decisions.reason: "Look, please" introduces a request made with some urgency or politeness; Abram is about to ask something of Sarai.

decisions.choice: a beautiful woman: Sarai's beauty at sixty-five
decisions.reason: By 12:4 and 17:17 Sarai is about sixty-five; in these chapters people live far longer than later, and her beauty is part of the story.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יִרְא֤וּ אֹתָךְ֙ הַמִּצְרִ֔ים וְאָמְר֖וּ אִשְׁתּ֣וֹ זֹ֑את וְהָרְג֥וּ אֹתִ֖י וְאֹתָ֥ךְ יְחַיּֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when see you the Egyptians and say, his wife [is] this, and they will kill me, and you they will let live.
pieces: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'She is his wife,' and they will kill me and keep you alive.

L.12: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This [is] his wife,' and they will kill me, but they will let you live.

R.12: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'She is his wife.' Then they will kill me and keep you.

records.source: אִמְרִי־נָ֖א אֲחֹ֣תִי אָ֑תְּ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יִֽיטַב־לִ֣י בַעֲבוּרֵ֔ךְ וְחָיְתָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י בִּגְלָלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Say, please, my sister [are] you, so that it may go well for me because of you, and my life will live on account of you.
pieces: Please tell them you are my sister. Then things will go well for me because of you, and I will stay alive thanks to you."

L.13: Please say you [are] my sister, so that it may go well with me because of you, and that my life may be spared on account of you."

R.13: Please tell them you are my sister. Then they will treat me well because of you, and they will not kill me."

decisions.choice: say you are my sister: a half-truth told out of fear
decisions.reason: Sarai was Abram's half-sister (20:12), so the words are partly true, but they are meant to deceive. Abram, who obeyed God's call, now acts out of fear and puts Sarai at risk. The narrator reports it without excuse; the same thing happens again in chapter 20, and with Isaac in chapter 26.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י כְּב֥וֹא אַבְרָ֖ם מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיִּרְא֤וּ הַמִּצְרִים֙ אֶת־הָ֣אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־יָפָ֥ה הִ֖וא מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And it was, as Abram entered Egypt, and saw the Egyptians the woman that beautiful she [was] very.
pieces: And so it was: as soon as Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how very beautiful the woman was.

L.14: And it happened, when Abram came into Egypt, that the Egyptians saw that the woman [was] very beautiful.

R.14: When Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֹתָהּ֙ שָׂרֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַיְהַֽלְל֥וּ אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַתֻּקַּ֥ח הָאִשָּׁ֖ה בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And saw her [the] officials of Pharaoh and praised her to Pharaoh, and was taken the woman [to the] house of Pharaoh.
pieces: Pharaoh's officials saw her too and spoke highly of her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into his palace.

L.15: And Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.

R.15: Pharaoh's officials saw her too, and they told Pharaoh how beautiful she was. So Sarai was taken to live in Pharaoh's palace.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh: the title of the king of Egypt
decisions.reason: Pharaoh is a title, "great house", not a personal name. The text does not say which king of Egypt this was.

decisions.choice: taken into Pharaoh's house: taken as a wife
decisions.reason: Being taken into Pharaoh's house means being taken into his household of wives (verse 19). The promise of a son through Sarai is in danger.

records.source: וּלְאַבְרָ֥ם הֵיטִ֖יב בַּעֲבוּרָ֑הּ וַֽיְהִי־ל֤וֹ צֹאן־וּבָקָר֙ וַחֲמֹרִ֔ים וַעֲבָדִים֙ וּשְׁפָחֹ֔ת וַאֲתֹנֹ֖ת וּגְמַלִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And to Abram he did good because of her, and there were to him sheep and cattle and male donkeys and male slaves and female slaves and female donkeys and camels.
pieces: Because of her, Pharaoh was generous to Abram, who came to own sheep, cattle and donkeys, male and female servants, she-donkeys and camels.

L.16: And he treated Abram well for her sake, and he had sheep and cattle and male donkeys, male slaves and female slaves, female donkeys and camels.

R.16: Pharaoh treated Abram well because of Sarai. He gave Abram sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels and servants, both men and women.

decisions.choice: he treated Abram well for her sake: wealth gained by the deception
decisions.reason: Abram's plan works: he grows rich (verse 13). But the gifts come at Sarai's expense, and the story does not praise him for them.

decisions.choice: male and female servants
decisions.reason: "Male and female servants" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; Literal keeps "male and female slaves".

records.source: וַיְנַגַּ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה׀אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֛ה נְגָעִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים וְאֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ עַל־דְּבַ֥ר שָׂרַ֖י אֵ֥שֶׁת אַבְרָֽם׃
records.gloss: And struck YHWH Pharaoh [with] plagues great, and his house, on account of [the] matter of Sarai, [the] wife of Abram.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram's wife Sarai.

L.17: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Pharaoh and his household with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.

R.17: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent terrible diseases on Pharaoh and the people in his palace because he had taken Sarai, Abram's wife.

decisions.choice: plagues on Pharaoh: a foretaste of the exodus
decisions.reason: "Plagues" (literally "strokes") is the word used of the last plague on Egypt (Exodus 11:1). Abram's descent to Egypt, the plagues and his being sent away with great wealth (verse 20) foreshadow Israel's story in Exodus.

decisions.choice: because of Sarai, Abram's wife: God protects the promise
decisions.reason: The LORD steps in to protect Sarai, and with her the promise of descendants, when Abram has failed to. The text does not say how Pharaoh learned the reason.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ לְאַבְרָ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֑י לָ֚מָּה לֹא־הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י כִּ֥י אִשְׁתְּךָ֖ הִֽוא׃
records.gloss: And summoned Pharaoh Abram and said, what [is] this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that your wife she [was]?
pieces: Pharaoh called for Abram and said, "What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me she was your wife?

L.18: And Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What [is] this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she [was] your wife?

R.18: So Pharaoh sent for Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?

decisions.choice: what is this you have done: the question God asked in 3:13
decisions.reason: Pharaoh asks the question God put to the woman in the garden (3:13). The foreign king rebukes the man of faith.

records.source: לָמָ֤ה אָמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֔וא וָאֶקַּ֥ח אֹתָ֛הּ לִ֖י לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֥ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֖ קַ֥ח וָלֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Why did you say, my sister [is] she, and I took her for myself for a wife? And now, behold your wife; take [her] and go.
pieces: Why did you claim she was your sister, and let me take her as my wife? Here she is. Take your wife and go!"

L.19: Why did you say, 'She [is] my sister,' so that I took her for my wife? Now then, here is your wife; take [her] and go."

R.19: Why did you say, 'She is my sister'? I took her to be my wife! Now here is your wife. Take her and go!"

decisions.choice: I took her for my wife: Pharaoh had married her
alternatives: I was about to take her
decisions.reason: The verb most naturally means that Pharaoh had taken Sarai as his wife. The text does not say more; in the parallel story of 20:4-6 God keeps the king from touching her.

records.source: וַיְצַ֥ו עָלָ֛יו פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And commanded about him Pharaoh men, and they sent him away and his wife and all that [was] to him.
pieces: Pharaoh put men in charge of Abram, and they escorted him out of the country with his wife and all his possessions.

L.20: And Pharaoh gave orders to men concerning him, and they sent him away, with his wife and all that he had.

R.20: Then Pharaoh ordered his men to send Abram away, with his wife and everything he owned.

decisions.choice: sent him away: the verb of the exodus
decisions.reason: "Sent away" is the verb Moses uses in "let my people go" (Exodus 5:1). Abram leaves Egypt with his wife and his wealth, as Israel later would (Exodus 12:35-36).
